objective: Build the JOINT null -- one carrying the cross-cell dependence the physical process has and both existing nulls omit -- and re-test the low-occupancy deficit and the model-free dispersion statistic against it. This is the single largest remaining threat to the only surviving positive finding in this lane: a sub-Poisson deficit measured against an independence-assuming null is exactly what cross-cell negative dependence would produce. Zero new sampling.

handoff.objective:
TWO JOBS, both zero new sampling.

JOB A -- THE JOINT NULL, which is the point of the batch. BATCH-017's validator established that N2 is the PER-CELL minimum-variance member and NOT the joint one: it is independent across cells, while the physical process couples cells within an iteration, and NEITHER N1 NOR N2 carries any cross-cell dependence. Build a null that does. The natural construction is to resample WHOLE ITERATIONS -- a multinomial allocation across cells that preserves each iteration's total -- but you own the choice; state what dependence structure your null carries and why it is the right one for a cumulative counting process. Then re-run against it the two statistics that currently carry the finding: (i) the 164-cell low-occupancy test, which reads mean t = 0.6811 against 0.9959 +/- 0.1084 (N1) and 0.9995 +/- 0.1114 (N2), z = -2.91 and -2.86; and (ii) the MODEL-FREE linearly-detrended var/mean, 0.453, 0.561 and 0.660 on the last 25, 50 and 100 cells of n=43 against an expectation of 1 with sampling sd 0.29, 0.20 and 0.14. THE MODEL-FREE STATISTIC MATTERS MOST because it needs no rate model, so if the deficit dies against a joint null the mechanism is cross-cell dependence, and if it survives, the finding stands on ground no null-family objection reaches.

JOB B -- BREAK THE CONFOUND AS FAR AS THE DESIGN ALLOWS. BATCH-017 W-8 records that occupancy is a near-monotone function of the score index over both bands (3 non-monotone steps in 300 for n=43, 0 in 495 for n=50), so an occupancy effect and any smooth score-position effect are PERFECTLY CONFOUNDED within a file. The two files map occupancy onto position differently -- max occupancy 0.739 for n=43 against 0.227 for n=50 -- so cells matched on POSITION but differing in OCCUPANCY across the two files partially break it. Report how far it can be broken and how far it cannot. A clean negative -- 'this design cannot separate them, here is why' -- is a perfectly good outcome and must not be dressed up.
handoff.uncertainty_reduced: Whether the sub-Poisson deficit is a property of the DATA or of the INDEPENDENCE ASSUMPTION in the null family it has been measured against; and whether occupancy can be separated from score position at all in this design.
